body:
## Summary

Refuse typed metadata acquisition from dtplyr root table subclasses before truncation can dispatch a caller method. This applies to typed Grouping-plan inspection and both Nest verbs, including derived inputs and every contributing root.

```diff
 dtplyr typed metadata preparation
+  verify every root has the ordinary data.table class vector
   truncate isolated roots only after metadata safety succeeds
```

Closes #1382.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the new focused inspection regression on main's implementation failed: subclass truncation received two populated source rows and typed inspection returned without the required safe refusal.
  **After:** the focused root-metadata file passes. Regressions independently cover empty-output retyping, reference mutation, native collection/grouping, name-only inspection, ordinary typed schema and Nest partitions, Mutable-step Nest refusal, and both graph-input positions.
- Verification: [full Review-ready, exact SHA and timing disposition](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1392#issuecomment-6680183873).
- Review: [Standards 0 / Spec 0; independent gpt-6.1-sol xhigh agents](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1392#issuecomment-6680222180).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reversible admission check; no dependency or stored-data migration.

**Blast Radius:** dtplyr

Typed metadata calls now conservatively refuse all root table subclasses, including subclasses without custom truncation methods. Explicitly collect and pass the resulting data frame to use typed selections. Name-only inspection, ordinary data.table roots, and the Mutable-step Nest refusal retain their behavior.
